headline: National Cricket Board mandates 40-hour work week for fans to ensure 'full-time support' during off-season
body:
The national cricket board announced today that all registered fans must now clock in at least 40 hours a week of engagement, including mandatory study sessions on pitch maps and deep-dive analysis of domestic tournament strike rates to prevent a dip in viewership metrics.

"It was observed that during the two-month gap between major leagues, fans were dangerously close to developing interest in other activities, such as reading books or interacting with their families," said board spokesperson Rajesh Varma. "This new policy ensures that the national discourse remains firmly locked on hypothetical team combinations, even when there isn't a ball being bowled anywhere in the world."

Under the new guidelines, fans will be required to submit weekly reports via a mobile application, proving they have spent at least twelve hours arguing on social media about the selection criteria for a tournament that is still six months away. Those who fail to meet the quota will face a suspension of their streaming privileges and a temporary ban on purchasing official team jerseys.

Independent analysts have lauded the initiative, noting that the national economy is essentially tethered to the emotional stability of the fan base. "If the average citizen isn't constantly stressed about the middle-order batting collapse of a franchise, consumer spending on stress-relief snacks and sedative teas will plummet," explained market strategist Anjali Iyer.
caption: New rules issued today ensure that your devotion to the sport doesn't falter just because there’s no match on TV. Stay focused, stay stressed. #CricketFans #NationalDuty #GameOn #OffSeasonGrind
